# Taṇhuppāda Sutta (Iti 105 (It 4.6 PTS It 109))
**ID:** Iti 105 (It 4.6 PTS It 109)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Taṇhuppāda Sutta
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/iti105
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Taṇhuppāda Sutta* ("The Arising of Craving", Iti 105) is the sixth discourse in the fourth section (Catukkanipāta) of the *Itivuttaka* [SuttaCentral; Windisch 1889]. The discourse identifies four grounds or occasions for the arising of craving in a monastic (*cattāro taṇhuppādā*): craving arising on account of robes (*cīvara-hetu*), almsfood (*piṇḍapāta-hetu*), lodging (*senāsana-hetu*), and becoming or non-becoming (*itibhavābhava-hetu*) [Windisch 1889]. This prose teaching is concluded by a verse declaring that a person with craving as a companion (*taṇhādutiyo puriso*) wanders in *saṁsāra* for an extended duration and fails to transcend the round of existence, cycling between varied states of becoming (*itthabhāvaññathābhāvaṁ*) [Windisch 1889]. The textual formula regarding craving for states of existence (*itibhavābhavahetu taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati*) is also cited in Buddhist Sanskrit scholastic traditions, where the *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* and its commentary analyze its equivalent (*itibhavavibhavahetos tṛṣṇā*) [de La Vallée Poussin, Abhidharmakośabhāṣyam].
SuttaCentral lists curated parallels to the discourse in AN 4.9 (which shares the title *Taṇhuppādasutta*), Iti 15 (*Taṇhāsaṁyojana Sutta*), Snp 3.12 (*Dvayatānupassanā Sutta*), and the *Mahāvāṇijajātaka* (Ja 493), along with northern parallels in a Sanskrit *Ekottarikāgama* fragment (SF 199) and Chinese translation T 765.2 [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis via DharmaNexus registers 69 Pali text-reuse matches across 16 texts, confirming that the full discourse is shared with AN 4.9 (§2.1–4.4 ↔ AN 4 §9.0.3–9.3.4 with 0.95 similarity) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, the verse portion (§3.1–4.4) recurs verbatim or near-verbatim in Snp 3.12 (§28.1–29.4), the canonical Niddesa treatises (*Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa*, Cnd 23; *Sāriputtasuttaniddesa*, Mnd 16), and commentaries on the *Apadāna*, *Suttanipāta*, *Cūḷaniddesa*, and *Itivuttaka* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also identifies an alignment between this text and the Sanskrit *Patna Dharmapada* [DharmaNexus].
